answer: At the network summit each agent submits a zk‑nullifier derived from a one‑time biometric proof, which the consensus prism hashes into a unique plume‑shaped commitment; the nullifier can be verified without revealing the underlying identity, and any reuse instantly invalidates the proof. Because the proof is minted only once per human, an attacker must acquire a fresh biometric token and lock a stake of 10 PoA tokens for each fabricated identity, forfeiting the stake if the nullifier collides.
